in: Bound Churning the Mill (Baddha Chakki Chalanasana)

s: A long yin twist catching the top foot behind while the legs scissor. Combines rotation with a quadriceps stretch.
Revolved chair with palms in prayer and the lower elbow hooked outside the opposite knee. The deepest of the standing twists.
in: Chair Pose with Prayer Twist (Parivrtta Utkatasana (namaskar))

s: A gentle seated rotation using the chair back for leverage. Safe for almost every body.
Seated with hands on the shoulders, twisting rhythmically side to side with the breath.
A seated spinal twist performed in a chair. The accessible version for offices, older practitioners and limited mobility.
Seated with legs wide, hands clasped, circling the torso as if turning a millstone. A classical abdominal and waist practice.
High lunge with the torso rotated and the opposite elbow to the outer knee. A common vinyasa transition and a genuine detoxifying twist.
Crescent Lunge Twist taken with a block under the supporting hand or beneath the seat. The prop shortens the distance to the floor so the spine can stay long instead of rounding to reach it.
in: Crescent Lunge Twist with Block (Parivrtta Ashta Chandrasana (block))

s: A seated shape with one hip internally and one externally rotated. Works both rotations of the hip at once.
Downward dog with one hand crossing to catch the opposite ankle.
in: Downward Dog with Twist (Parivrtta Adho Mukha Svanasana)

s: Seated with legs extended, twisting side to side to reach the opposite foot. A warming spinal rotation.
The bound full expression of the seated twist with the arms wrapping the leg. Requires shoulder range as much as spinal rotation.
in: Full Lord of the Fishes (Paripurna Matsyendrasana)

s: Full Lord of the Fishes taken with a block under the supporting hand or beneath the seat. The prop shortens the distance to the floor so the spine can stay long instead of rounding to reach it.
in: Full Lord of the Fishes with Block (Paripurna Matsyendrasana (block))

s: A deep squat with the arms binding around the legs in a twist. Demands ankle range before rotation is even possible.
Extended puppy with one arm threading beneath the body into a thoracic rotation.
Reclined pigeon taken across the body into a twist. Releases the outer hip and low back together.
Legs extended and swept to one side while the shoulders stay down. Stronger on the obliques than the knees-bent version.
in: Reclined Twist with Extended Leg (Jathara Parivartanasana)

s: A supine twist held five minutes per side. The standard closing shape of a yin practice.
Chair pose with the torso rotated and the opposite elbow outside the knee. Combines leg endurance with a closed twist.
A seated side bend and twist over one straight leg with the top arm reaching overhead. Opens the side body more than the hamstrings.
A revolved low lunge with the arms binding beneath the front thigh.
Revolved side angle with a full bind. Rotation, leg endurance and shoulder opening at once.
in: Revolved Side Angle with Bind (Baddha Parivrtta Parsvakonasana)

s: Triangle with the torso rotated so the opposite hand reaches the floor. Balance and hamstring length are both tested at once.
A bound seated twist with the arm hooked outside the upright knee. The bind deepens the rotation well beyond the unbound version.
Sage Marichi III taken with a block under the supporting hand or beneath the seat. The prop shortens the distance to the floor so the spine can stay long instead of rounding to reach it.
in: Sage Marichi III with Block (Marichyasana III (block))

s: A bound seated twist with one leg in half lotus. The most demanding of the four Marichi poses.
The half lord of the fishes — one knee upright, torso rotating toward it. The reference seated twist of modern practice.
Seated Twist taken with a block under the supporting hand or beneath the seat. The prop shortens the distance to the floor so the spine can stay long instead of rounding to reach it.
A wide-legged seated position with the torso rotating and folding over one leg. Combines adductor stretch with rotation.
Seated Wide-Legged Twist taken with a block under the supporting hand or beneath the seat. The prop shortens the distance to the floor so the spine can stay long instead of rounding to reach it.
in: Seated Wide-Legged Twist with Block (Parivrtta Upavistha Konasana (block))

s: The closing twist of the Bikram series, taken with a specific hand and knee placement.
Loose rotational swinging of the torso with the arms trailing. A classical warm-up from the pawanmuktasana series.
The wide-legged fold with one hand to the floor and the other reaching up in rotation.
Knees dropping to one side while the shoulders stay grounded. The gentlest twist available and the standard closing shape before savasana.
From all fours, one arm threading beneath the body to the opposite side. Releases the upper back and rear shoulder with no strain.
The revolved triangle of the Ashtanga sequence, entered from a specific foot alignment.
Warrior I with the torso rotating over the front thigh. Strong legs beneath a closed twist, and hard on the sacroiliac joint if forced.
Warrior I Twist taken with a block under the supporting hand or beneath the seat. The prop shortens the distance to the floor so the spine can stay long instead of rounding to reach it.
in: Warrior I Twist with Block (Parivrtta Virabhadrasana (block))

s: Knees falling slowly side to side with the feet planted. The gentlest possible spinal rotation.
